newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close down on Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close down on Iraq news.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed down but off lows on Tuesday following the U.S missile strike on Iraq, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 4.48 points, or 0.82 percent, to 540.54 points after tumbling to 536.41 points early in the afternoon session.
Losers led gainers by 74 to 27, with 43 counters unchanged.
Brokers said there was short-selling by foreigners of selected blue-chip stocks after news of the missile strike, but they described it as a knee-jerk reaction.

"The news of the U.S strike had hit the market in the early afternoon session, but it then rebounded slightly in late trade as the market realised there was no immediate or direct impact to Indonesia's economy," said one foreign broker.
He added that the market was quiet since morning as many operators were awaiting upcoming U.S economic data.
Another foreign broker said a reasoned response to the missile strike would be available on Wednesday after brokers got a lead from Wall Street.
Heavyweights Telkom, Semen Gresik and Sampoerna were among the losers in the fall-out of the missile strike news.
Telecommunications firm Telkom fell 25 rupiah to 3,275 on a turnover of 2.5 million shares while Semen Gresik fell 175 rupiah to 6,150 on a volume of 1.2 million shares.
Secondliner duty-free shop operator Sona Topas Tour topped the active list with 7.1 million shares traded, rising 25 rupiah to 1,025 on what brokers said was speculative buying.
